meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but; so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('necessary, needed').
Common feminine noun meaning 'flat, apartment' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Do you remember the toilet in the communal flat?

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'страивать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to organize, arrange', paired with 'устроить'.

examples.text: Мне нужно как-то устраивать новую жизнь.
examples.trans: I need to arrange a new life somehow.

examples.text: Богатая дама устраивает банкет своей собачке.
examples.trans: A rich lady is throwing a banquet for her little dog.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?
And this is for you. A toy car!

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Муж тоже там работал. И рано умер.
examples.trans: My husband worked there too. And he died young.
Tomorrow I need to get up early.

examples.text: Что, по домам? Мне завтра рано вставать.
examples.trans: What, time to go home? I have to get up early tomorrow.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'can, to be able', paired with 'смочь'.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to get in the way'.

related.gloss: to to get in the way (prefixed perfective)
not to to get in the way (negated infinitive)

examples.trans: What, could it get in the way?

examples.text: На кухне никто не хочет мешаться без причины.
examples.trans: In the kitchen nobody wants to get in the way without a reason.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'well; come on', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'on, onto; for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'смотреть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to have a look', paired with 'смотреть'.

examples.trans: Can I go and have a look?

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to come, to arrive', paired with 'приходить'.

examples.trans: Security will be here any moment.

examples.text: Не надо, Самсон. Сейчас придёт охрана.
examples.trans: Don't, Samson. Security will be here any second.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'work, job' in everyday Russian.
High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'about', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'говориться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to agree, to arrange', paired with 'договариваться'.

examples.text: Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'how; as', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'амочувствие'). Common neuter noun meaning 'health, physical state, well-being' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я хотела узнать, как ваше самочувствие.
examples.trans: I wanted to know how you are feeling.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'your', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?
Tell us, when will your programme be out?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'so, then; like that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, that; it is', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning '(emphasis) after all, but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.
And does the governor support you?

examples.text: Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to want', paired with 'захотеть'.

examples.trans: If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'просить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to ask', paired with 'спрашивать'.

examples.text: А спросите у него, куда он дел компьютерный класс.
examples.trans: Ask him where he put the computer lab.

examples.text: Да? А спросите у него, куда он дел компьютерный класс.
examples.trans: Really? Then ask him where he put the computer lab.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'my, mine', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'no; there isn't', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'лноваться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to worry'.

дождаться.gloss: to wait for, to live to see

meanings.en: to wait for, to live to see
meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'ждаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to wait for, to live to see', paired with 'дожидаться'.

examples.trans: I will wait for an answer.

examples.text: Я всё равно дождусь твоего ответа!
examples.trans: I will wait for your answer anyway!

examples.text: Я готов спокойно дождаться решения суда.
examples.trans: I am ready to wait calmly for the court decision.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'result' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я жду только одного — результатов от вас.
examples.trans: I expect only one thing: results from you.
This is an excellent result of the work.

examples.text: Я жду только одного — результатов от вас. Работайте!
examples.trans: I expect only one thing: results from you. Get to work!

meanings.note: Classical Greek compound borrowing ('томография'), feminine noun. Common feminine noun meaning 'MRI scan' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Let us wait for the MRI results.

examples.text: На нашей кухне уже есть новая томография.
examples.trans: In our kitchen there is already a new MRI scan.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'from; of', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be required, be needed', paired with 'потребоваться'.

examples.trans: There, which is what needed to be proved!
Experience is required for this job.

examples.text: Что и требовалось доказать, Елена Павловна!
examples.trans: That proves my point, Elena Pavlovna!

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
High-frequency Russian cardinal or ordinal numeral meaning 'one', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'трого'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: The teacher looked at us sternly.

examples.text: Нет, я нормально его пугал, строго!
examples.trans: No, I scared him properly, sternly!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'облюдать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to observe, comply with', paired with 'соблюсти'.

examples.trans: It is important to keep quiet.

examples.text: Тогда соблюдайте режим и не нарушайте.
examples.trans: Then observe the regime and do not violate it.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'regime, routine, mode' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: There is a strict hospital regime here.

examples.text: Здесь строгий режим и нельзя громко шуметь.
examples.trans: There is a strict regime here and one cannot make loud noise.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'делать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to do, to make', paired with 'делать'.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything, all; that's it', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'зможно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Возможно, вы любите есть сырую рыбу.
examples.trans: Perhaps, you like to eat raw fish.

examples.text: Как это сегодня вечером? Это невозможно!
examples.trans: What do you mean, this evening? That's impossible!

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'деяться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to hope, to rely on', paired with 'понадеяться'.

examples.trans: I hope so. Go on, act quickly!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'коро'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Так, не шумим. Я скоро вернусь.
examples.trans: Right, no noise. I'll be back soon.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'we', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

покинуть.gloss: to leave, to vacate, to abandon

meanings.en: to leave, to vacate, to abandon
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'кинуть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to leave, to vacate, to abandon', paired with 'покидать'.

examples.trans: What is the matter? Leave the operating room!
